atom_types.name: caps_ua_ch_s1_bCH_aCH_dCH_iCH
atom_types.description: CAPS CH on a sulfide S (by_analogy: the 1986 table's carbon-on-sulfide charge +0.235, which CH3 90 and CH2 91 share, with the 1984 sp3 CH's Lennard-Jones 73)

atom_types.name: caps_ua_ch_s2_bCH_aCH_dCH_iCH
atom_types.description: CAPS CH on an S bonded to S (by_analogy: the carbon-on-disulfide charge +0.30 of CH3 92 and CH2 93, with the sp3 CH's Lennard-Jones 73)

atom_types.name: caps_ua_ch_sh_bCH_aCH_dCH_iCH
atom_types.description: CAPS CH on a thiol S (by_analogy: the carbon-on-thiol charge +0.18 of CH3 88 and CH2 89, with the sp3 CH's Lennard-Jones 73)

atom_types.name: caps_ua_s_poly_bS~_aS~_dS~_iS~
atom_types.description: CAPS S between two S, a polysulfide's middle S (by_analogy: the disulfide S's Lennard-Jones 85; each end S is balanced by its carbon, so the middle S carries 0)

atom_types.name: caps_ua_s_ssh_bSH_aSH_dSH_iSH
atom_types.description: CAPS persulfide S-H sulfur (by_analogy: the thiol S's Lennard-Jones 83; with the thiol H 87 (+0.27) the S-H group is neutral, the rest of the chain balanced by the disulfide numbers)

notes: the united-atom carbon sites carry their hydrogens' mass (CH4 16.043, CH3 15.035, CH2 14.027, CH 13.019)

110 bends and 908 torsions the 2024 file lacks for united-atom hydrocarbons, alcohols and ethers, from Jorgensen, Madura & Swenson, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 106, 6638 (1984), Tables I and II; Jorgensen, J. Phys. Chem. 90, 1276 (1986), Tables II and III; Briggs, Matsui & Jorgensen, J. Comput. Chem. 11, 958 (1990), Table II and p. 960 (bench/ff/open/oplsua2024_supplement.json; each term's comment names its table and anything taken from the 2024 file); the 2024 file's own terms win

the papers' torsions were fit with fixed bond lengths and angles, no 1-4 Lennard-Jones and weak terms beyond 1-4 (1984 eq 3: C-C sigma 4 A, epsilon 0.0074; 1986: HO-CH3 sigma 2.6 A, epsilon 0.008; 1990 eq 3: sigma 2.745 A, epsilon 0.008 kcal/mol); here they run with the 2024 file's flexible bonds and its 1-4 x 0.5 scaling

none of the three papers has a torsion about a C-C bond between two oxygens (O-C-C-O: poly(ethylene oxide), glycols) or an O-C-O acetal term; those are CAPS's fits to RI-MP2/cc-pVTZ//HF/6-31G** relaxed scans of all-atom fragments (1,2-dimethoxyethane, 2-methoxyethanol, acetal and glycidyl-ether fragments) with the united-atom model evaluated on them (caps.torsionfit), each comment giving its RMS; hydroxyl torsions whose scans are dominated by an intramolecular OH...O hydrogen bond (RMS over 1.1 kcal/mol) are not fitted and stay missing

bonds.name: CH-S~
bonds.comment: Jorgensen, J. Phys. Chem. 90, 6379 (1986), as the 2024 file gives it: by_analogy: C2-S~ / C3-S~ 222 / 1.81 for every sp3 carbon on a sulfide or disulfide S (the 1986 paper uses one C-S bond for any alkyl group; the crosslink CH has no entry)

bonds.name: CH-SH
bonds.comment: Jorgensen, J. Phys. Chem. 90, 6379 (1986), as the 2024 file gives it: by_analogy: C2-SH / C3-SH 222 / 1.81 for every sp3 carbon on a thiol S

bonds.name: SH-S~
bonds.comment: Jorgensen, J. Phys. Chem. 90, 6379 (1986), as the 2024 file gives it: by_analogy: the disulfide S-S bond S~-S~ 166 / 2.038 for an S-S bond to a persulfide S-H sulfur

dihedrals.name: C3-C2-CH-C3
dihedrals.comment: Jorgensen, Madura & Swenson 1984, Table II (isopentane), per torsion: the paper gives isopentane's rotation about its CH-CH2 bond as one function of phi (V0 2.713, V1 1.526, V2 0.533, V3 -3.453), phi = 0 where the CH2's carbon is gauche to both carbons on the CH. The two C-CH-CH2-C torsions sit at phi + 60 and phi - 60, so V1' = V1, V2' = -V2 and V3' = -V3/2 on each reproduce the paper's function exactly up to a constant (with three-fold symmetry at the CH). Every CH-CH2 bond in a united-atom chain has the same two torsions
